title: DAGonStore: Reliable Data Management for Workflows on the Computing Continuum with DynoStore and DAGonStar
problem: The computing continuum (edge-to-cloud) brings computation near data sources but introduces data management challenges: ensuring data availability/reliability across heterogeneous, failure-prone, distributed storage nodes while maintaining consistency.
motivation: Computing continuum paradigm enables low-latency processing but lacks robust data management. Distributed systems naturally encounter node failures, network partitions, and disconnections. Workflow engines need resilient, location-transparent data access.
method: DAGonStore stores workflow data across edge-to-cloud systems by splitting it into redundant pieces using erasure codes—a technique where you break data into fragments so the full data can be recovered even if some storage nodes fail. It distributes these pieces using utilization-aware load-balancing, which watches how full each storage node is and spreads the load to prevent any single node from getting overwhelmed. The system was tested for scalability across many nodes, fault tolerance when storage nodes fail, and how little manual work users need to do.
key_novelty: The core idea is combining erasure codes with utilization-aware load-balancing so workflow data stays available even when storage nodes fail across edge-to-cloud systems.
contributions: DAGonStore: data management layer for computing continuum workflows
Integration with DynoStore for wide-area storage
Automatic failure handling and data recovery
Demonstration of scalable fault-tolerant workflow execution

metrics.fault_tolerance: demonstrated under node failures and disconnections

limitations: Limited scalability evaluation (system size not specified). Overhead of erasure codes not quantified. Comparison with other fault-tolerance approaches missing. Applicability to latency-sensitive workloads unclear.
primary_theme: Fault-tolerant data management for edge-to-cloud workflows
